citations.assessment: Yoma 9a gives Yochanan ben Torta on why Shiloh was destroyed. Both commentators cited in Heilprin gloss this line. The received ע׳ א׳ is kept as evidence.
The Yerushalmi has Yochanan bar Torta about the desecration of festivals and sacred offerings. Its reasons remain distinct from the Bavli’s wording.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The commentary relates the conversion story and explicitly reports the Yehudah variant in Pesikta Rabbati.
Pesikta Rabbati 14 recounts the conversion and in the checked text names him Yochanan. Yehudah remains the reading reported by Tosafot Yeshanim.
Ritva explicitly attributes the sale, refusal to plow and whisper to the Yerushalmi.
Heilprin’s Huna bar Torta entry is the first requested internal notice.
Heilprin’s Chanina entry explicitly cross-refers to the Huna and Yochanan notices. The shared epithet does not establish identity.
Yochanan declined Akiva’s request because he had not reviewed the Torah passage, and the sages praised him.
The midrash supplies the rebuke to Akiva regarding Bar Koziva and the Yerushalmi parallel names the son of David explicitly.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: Tosefta explicitly gives Yochanan ben Torta and blames contempt for sacred offerings at Shiloh.

holds.reason: The Pesikta text checked here differs from the form quoted in Tosafot Yeshanim. A print witness for that quoted form remains open.
The attribution is verified in Ritva. The checked Yerushalmi Yoma comparison gives the Shiloh dictum, while the direct Yerushalmi locus for the cow anecdote remains open.
